cues.en: He cannot be allowed to leave this place.
cues.zh: 绝不能让他离开这里。

cues.en: He will need everything.
cues.zh: 他会不惜一切代价。

cues.en: I'm willing to take full responsibility
cues.zh: 我愿意承担全部责任，

cues.en: for the horrible events of the last twenty four hours, but you must understand.
cues.zh: 对过去 24 小时内发生的惨剧负责，但你们必须明白。

cues.en: Our interest in their world was purely for the betterment of mankind.
cues.zh: 我们探索他们的世界，纯粹是为了人类的福祉。

cues.en: Everything has clearly gotten out of hand now. Yes.
cues.zh: 显然，现在一切都失控了，确实。

cues.en: But it was worth the risk.
cues.zh: 但冒这个险是值得的。

cues.en: I assure you.
cues.zh: 我向你们保证。

cues.en: Good evening, everybody.
cues.zh: 大家晚上好。

cues.en: I tell you, I'm so happy to be speaking to you all this evening. This is absolutely brilliant.
cues.zh: 跟大家说，今晚能在这里和各位交流我太高兴了，这感觉棒极了。

cues.en: I'm really really happy to be speaking to you all one because I know it's 05:00 on Wednesday afternoon so I can guarantee that at least thirty percent of you are sober.
cues.zh: 我之所以特别高兴能和大家聊，首先是因为现在是周三下午五点，我敢打赌在座至少有三成的人还是清醒的。

cues.en: The second thing is that I really have not had a chance to geek out on those wonderful details that went into the Godoom soundtrack like I will tonight. So if you're here for those sort of geeky details, that's really what we're gonna get into. Let's get started.
cues.zh: 第二点是，我一直没机会像今晚这样，好好深挖一下《Doom》原声带里那些极客细节。所以如果你是冲着这些硬核细节来的，那正好是我们要聊的。我们开始吧。

cues.en: Have you ever received a brief
cues.zh: 你们有没有收到过这样一份需求，

cues.en: that went something like this?
cues.zh: 大概是写成这样的？

cues.en: We want you to make music that no one has ever heard before.
cues.zh: “我们希望你做出一首前所未闻的音乐。

cues.en: It needs to fit the game perfectly
cues.zh: 它必须与游戏完美契合，

cues.en: and be instantly loved by millions of fans.
cues.zh: 并且立刻收获数百万粉丝的喜爱。”

cues.en: Now, if you're anything like me,
cues.zh: 要是你们跟我差不多的话，

cues.en: when you get a brief like that, your initial reaction is to run into the bathroom, pour the cold tap on, crawl up into a little ball, and have a little cry.
cues.zh: 拿到这种需求时，第一反应肯定是一头扎进洗手间，打开冷水龙头，缩成一团哭上一场。

cues.en: But what I'm gonna talk to you about tonight is how you can execute a brief like this, and I'm gonna discuss with you the lessons that I learned to enable you to do so.
cues.zh: 但我今晚想讲的，是如何搞定这样的需求，并分享我一路走来总结的经验，希望能对你们有所启发。

cues.en: I first met the id Software team back in about mid twenty fourteen.
cues.zh: 我第一次接触 id Software 团队是在 2014 年年中左右。

cues.en: They sent me a music design document that started like this.
cues.zh: 他们发给我一份音乐设计文档，开头是这么写的：

cues.en: Doom is about demons on Mars. You have a shotgun. Send them back to hell.
cues.zh: “《Doom》讲的是火星上的恶魔。你手里有把霰弹枪。把它们轰回地狱去。”

cues.en: Cool.
cues.zh: 酷。

cues.en: The second part of the brief went like this.
cues.zh: 需求的第二部分是这样的：

cues.en: No guitars.
cues.zh: “不要吉他。

cues.en: We hate guitars. We do not want guitars in our game. Do not put guitars in.
cues.zh: 我们讨厌吉他。我们游戏里绝对不能有吉他。千万别加吉他。”

cues.en: Underneath that big section was a little line that said, I love synths.
cues.zh: 在那一大段字下面，有一行小字写着：“我喜欢合成器。”

cues.en: Cool? I can work with that.
cues.zh: 酷吧？这我还能应付。

cues.en: The third part of this brief went like this.
cues.zh: 需求的第三部分则是这样：

cues.en: We want you to create music that nobody's ever heard before.
cues.zh: “我们希望你创作出前所未有的音乐。

cues.en: It needs to fit the game perfectly
cues.zh: 它要与游戏完美契合，

cues.en: and instantly loved by millions of fans.
cues.zh: 并且立刻赢得数百万粉丝的心。”

cues.en: Now, Doom fans, they're not like Disney fans.
cues.zh: 要知道，《Doom》的粉丝可不像迪士尼粉丝那么好伺候。

cues.en: If Doom fans don't like what you've done, they'll burn your house down.
cues.zh: 要是《Doom》粉丝不喜欢你的作品，他们会把你的房子给点了。

cues.en: So let's say we take a brief like this, right, and we hand it to a piano player.
cues.zh: 那么假设我们拿到这样一份需求，交到一个钢琴演奏家手里。

cues.en: Now this piano player is gonna channel in the demons
cues.zh: 这位钢琴家会试图代入恶魔的意象，

cues.en: and they're gonna channel in the hell and they're gonna channel in the Mars.
cues.zh: 代入地狱，代入火星。

cues.en: But what you're gonna end up with is a solo piano piece.
cues.zh: 但你最终得到的只会是一首钢琴独奏曲。

cues.en: It's inspired by the brief. Sure.
cues.zh: 它的灵感确实来自这份需求，没错。

cues.en: But it's not an a... An execution of the brief.
cues.zh: 但它根本没……没能真正落地执行这份需求。

cues.en: Now say you gave the same brief to a dubstep producer.
cues.zh: 假设你把同样的需求交给一位 Dubstep 制作人。

cues.en: This dubstep producer is gonna take all those awesome demon growling bases.
cues.zh: 这位 Dubstep 制作人会用上所有那些超炫的恶魔咆哮般的贝斯。

cues.en: They're gonna take some awesome bell samples to get the hell thing in there and they're gonna get mixed in some bra samples to get in the Mars thing. Right?
cues.zh: 他们会找些超棒的钟声采样来表现地狱元素，再混入一些铜管采样来体现火星元素，对吧？

cues.en: But what you're gonna end up with is a dubstep track.
cues.zh: 但你最终得到的还是一首 Dubstep 风格的曲子。

cues.en: It's inspired by the brief. Sure. It's got synths in there
cues.zh: 它的灵感确实来自这份需求，里面也有合成器，

cues.en: but it's not an execution
cues.zh: 但它并不是

cues.en: of the brief.
cues.zh: 对这份需求的真正落实。

cues.en: Now same again if you handed that exact same brief to a composer
cues.zh: 同理，如果你把完全相同的需求交给一位配乐师，

cues.en: and that composer's
cues.zh: 而那位配乐师的

cues.en: instant reaction is to open up their cubase template that they've worked with for the last 10 projects
cues.zh: 第一反应是打开他们过去十个项目都在用的 Cubase 模板，

cues.en: and they're gonna use all their daemon contact patches
cues.zh: 调出他们所有的恶魔 Kontakt 音色预设，

cues.en: and they're gonna use all their hell contact patches and they're gonna use all of their Mars contact patches,
cues.zh: 调出他们所有的地狱 Kontakt 音色预设，再调出所有的火星 Kontakt 音色预设，

cues.en: you're gonna get up with the... You're gonna end up with the same piece of music that that person has written for the last 10 projects.
cues.zh: 你最终得到的……最终得到的还是那个人在过去十个项目里写过的那种音乐。

cues.en: It's inspired by the brief, sure,
cues.zh: 确实，它的灵感来自需求，

cues.en: but it's not an execution of the brief.
cues.zh: 但并没有真正贯彻这份需求。

cues.en: Now why these three failed?
cues.zh: 那么，为什么这三者都失败了？

cues.en: The reason that they're failing in this example
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，他们失败的原因

cues.en: is that they're going through the exact same process that they've always done every single time.
cues.zh: 在于每一次他们都在重复完全相同的流程。

cues.en: And you cannot expect to end up with a different a different outcome
cues.zh: 如果不改变流程，

cues.en: without changing the process.
cues.zh: 你不可能期望得到一个不同的结果。

cues.en: Change the process,
cues.zh: 改变流程，

cues.en: change the outcome.
cues.zh: 才能改变结果。

cues.en: Now this is obviously a lot easier said than done. We're very fearful of changing the process.
cues.zh: 显然，这说起来容易做起来难。我们对改变流程充满了恐惧。

cues.en: If you're anything like me, you suffer terribly from the fear of rejection.
cues.zh: 如果你跟我一样，那你一定也深受“害怕被否定”的折磨。

cues.en: It's that fear of rejection
cues.zh: 正是这种害怕被否定的心理，

cues.en: that disables us from changing our process. Why?
cues.zh: 阻碍了我们改变流程。为什么？

cues.en: Because that's asking you to take everything you know and put it aside.
cues.zh: 因为这要求你把已知的一切都抛在一边。

cues.en: Come up with a new process in the hopes that you're going to reach something better.
cues.zh: 去摸索一套全新的流程，寄希望于做出更好的成果。

cues.en: Now as humans, we don't wanna do that. If something has worked a certain way before,
cues.zh: 作为人类，我们天生抗拒这样做。如果某种方法以前管用，

cues.en: we wanna repeat that process to end up with what we perceive is gonna be the same result. If it's gotten us a success in the in the past, we expect it's going to get us a success in the future.
cues.zh: 我们就想重复那个流程，去获得预料之中的相同结果。如果它过去带给我们成功，我们就期望它未来也能带来成功。

cues.en: But in the ever changing perpetual world that we live in, that's simply not the case.
cues.zh: 但在我们所处的这个瞬息万变的世界里，事实根本不是这样。

cues.en: Change the process, change the outcome.
cues.zh: 改变流程，改变结果。

cues.en: But the key to this is working with a team
cues.zh: 但这其中的关键，在于要和一个

cues.en: that shares this exact same philosophy.
cues.zh: 完全认同这种理念的团队共事。

cues.en: I was very excited to meet the Doom team. Ben picked me up from the hotel in Dallas and drove me all the way down to the Yid offices. The whole way he played this most incredible electronic music. It was great. It was all this weird sort of crazy like experimental stuff. There's no beat. There's no time signature. There's no nothing. It's just random sort of weirdness. But he listens to this stuff every morning to inspire him.
cues.zh: 当时能去见 DOOM 团队，我非常兴奋。Ben 到达拉斯的酒店接我，一路开车送我到 id 办公室。一路上他都在放那种极其不可思议的电子音乐。太棒了。全是些古怪、狂乱又实验性的东西。没有节拍，没有拍号，什么规则都没有，就是纯粹随机的怪声。但他每天早上都听这些东西来获取灵感。

cues.en: When I entered the office, I met Chad Mossolder. Chad was just finishing up the masters on his latest experimental
cues.zh: 我走进办公室时，遇到了 Chad Mossolder。Chad 正在完成他最新实验

cues.en: electronic music album, this one here. Richard Devine did a remix on it. It's really, really fantastic stuff. I was then introduced to Chris Hite, the audio director. Now Chris' room, couldn't even get into because it was full of synthesizers.
cues.zh: 电子音乐专辑的母带，就是这张。Richard Devine 给它做了混音。真的非常非常棒。之后有人把我介绍给音频总监 Chris Hite。Chris 的房间我根本进不去，因为里面塞满了合成器。

cues.en: There was synths everywhere. There was boxes of sounds everywhere. I couldn't move.
cues.zh: 到处都是合成器。到处都是装声音的箱子。我都没法动弹。

cues.en: Straight away after meeting Chris, I was told that there was a very, very, very, very important audio centric meeting. So we all rushed into a room.
cues.zh: 刚见完 Chris，我就被告知有一个非常非常非常非常重要的、以音频为核心的会议。于是我们都冲进了一个房间。

cues.en: You see, FX Twin had just dropped a couple of new tracks and we all had to have a listen.
cues.zh: 你看，FX Twin 刚发了几首新歌，我们都得去听一听。

cues.en: It was clear that these guys lived creativity
cues.zh: 很明显，这些人活着就是创意

cues.en: and they breathed creativity.
cues.zh: 呼吸也是创意。

cues.en: In fact, every Wednesday evening after work, they had this fantastic concept called weird Wednesday,
cues.zh: 事实上，每周三下班后，他们都有一个很棒的玩法，叫 Weird Wednesday，

cues.en: where they'd all get into a studio together and just geek out for a while on any new plug ins or any new pieces of equipment that they got and they just jam.
cues.zh: 大家会一起进录音室，花点时间钻研新插件或新设备，然后就即兴玩起来。

cues.en: Now they're not jamming the conventional sense. There's not a tempo. There's not a key signature that they sent to. They're not playing licks or anything.
cues.zh: 他们不是传统意义上的即兴。没有速度，也没有固定调号。他们不弹乐句之类的东西。

cues.en: Chad over there on the far right is running his guitar through his laptop and he's playing with all sorts of module modules, making all sorts of cool sounds.
cues.zh: 右边远处的 Chad 把吉他接进笔记本电脑，摆弄各种模块，做出各种很酷的声音。

cues.en: Ben in the middle there at the background, he had a Eurorack system and he was making all sorts of awesome incredible sounds with these make noise modules that he just picked up. That's Chris there on the left and he had his, Ableton Live set up and he was making all sorts of, you know, processing and sound design based on what the other two guys were doing. I had my little laptop set down up at the front here. And the guys would record this and they'd just jam away making all sorts of weird random sounds for two hours. And they'd record it for archival reasons, but that wasn't really the purpose.
cues.zh: Ben 在中间靠后的位置，他有一套 Eurorack 系统，正用刚入手的 Make Noise 模块做出各种惊艳的声音。左边是 Chris，他架好了 Ableton Live，根据另外两人的演奏做各种处理和声音设计。我把我那台小笔记本电脑放在前面这里。大家会把这一切录下来，然后就即兴玩上两个小时，制造各种奇怪随机的声音。他们录音是为了存档，但那并不是真正的目的。

cues.en: The purpose here was to break away from any creative inhibitions. It was to break away from anything that was stopping them from getting to their creativity.
cues.zh: 这里的目的，是打破一切创作上的束缚。是摆脱任何阻碍他们发挥创造力的东西。

cues.en: What they were doing was creating an environment
cues.zh: 他们所做的，是创造一个环境

cues.en: where each of them felt comfortable
cues.zh: 让每个人都能坦然地

cues.en: in failure.
cues.zh: 面对失败。

cues.en: So I was so inspired after you know hanging out with these guys for a couple of days and I couldn't wait to get back to my studio. Right? And I was like, okay, cool. I'm gonna come up with something like really really incredible, you know, creative, doom music based on synths and stuff. Right? So you know synths. Right, dude? So we got synths and there's hell. Right? And hell's down below. So you know, synths, we can put them down below like a sub. Yeah? So let's start with like a sub part. Right?
cues.zh: 和这些人混了几天后，我特别受启发，迫不及待想回自己的工作室。对吧？我就想，好，酷。我要做出点真正特别厉害、特别有创意、基于合成器之类的 doom 音乐。对吧？你懂合成器吧？对吧，哥们？我们有合成器，还有地狱。对吧？地狱在下面。所以，合成器嘛，我们可以把它们放到底下，像低频一样。对吧？那就从低频部分开始吧。对吧？

cues.en: Oh man. GDC speakers. Are you kidding me?
cues.zh: 天哪。GDC 的音响。逗我呢？

cues.en: That's what that sounds like. Okay. It's really low subpar. Right? But this is actually really good. See, trouble with subnotes is when you're running them so low as we demonstrated just then, you can't hear them.
cues.zh: 听起来就是那样。好吧，它真的很低，不太行。对吧？但这其实很不错。你看，低频音的问题在于，当你像刚才演示那样把它们开得那么低，你就听不到它们。

cues.en: So instead, we wanna take some high frequency content. We wanna add some high frequency content to those subparts
cues.zh: 所以反过来，我们要取一些高频内容。我们要给那些低频部分加入一些高频内容，

cues.en: in order to the, for the player to be able to hear them on their TV systems.
cues.zh: 以便玩家能在他们的电视系统上听到它们。

cues.en: Now one of the ways that I like to do this is to take white noise.
cues.zh: 我喜欢这样做的一种方法是取白噪声。

cues.en: And I take this white noise and I turn the white noise on and I turn the white noise off
cues.zh: 我拿这个白噪声，把白噪声打开，再把白噪声关闭，

cues.en: at a rate that mirrors the frequency of the sub underneath.
cues.zh: 以与下方低频相匹配的频率来开关。

cues.en: So what I'm essentially doing here is ring modulation. Right? But it's ring modulation at the audio frequency.
cues.zh: 所以我这里本质上做的是环形调制。对吧？但这是音频频率上的环形调制。

cues.en: Now the sub there that you couldn't even really hear was ringing at about 36.7
cues.zh: 现在你几乎听不到的那个低频，大约在 36.7

cues.en: hertz. So 36.7
cues.zh: 赫兹。所以 36.7

cues.en: times per second that that that's bouncing or trying to bounce. It wasn't really bouncing.
cues.zh: 次每秒，它在振动或试图振动。其实并没有真正振动。

cues.en: So when you take a a a like a white noise and you do that with the same sort of thing, you end up with this sound.
cues.zh: 所以当你取一个像白噪声这样的东西，用同样的方式处理，就会得到这个声音。

cues.en: Alright. So when you combine those two together and you get the sub and the white noise, you can hear them together. You're probably not gonna hear the full result on these speakers though.
cues.zh: 好。所以把两者结合起来，得到低频和白噪声，你就能一起听到它们。不过你可能不会在这些音箱上听到完整效果。

cues.en: There's the sub.
cues.zh: 这就是低频。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对吧。

cues.en: I feel we're really testing the GDC speakers here.
cues.zh: 我觉得我们真是在考验 GDC 的音响了。

cues.en: Now if you take this combination, you feed it through a distortion process, you get all sorts of really interesting harmonics. In the next video here, I'll run these two together through some distortion. You'll hear all sorts of interesting stuff start to happen. Now I'll turn the white noise off halfway through and you can hear what the distortion is doing to the sub alone, you'll and notice that the white noise is actually doing quite a lot.
cues.zh: 现在如果你把这个组合送进失真处理，你会得到各种非常有趣的谐波。在接下来的视频里，我会把这两个一起过一遍失真。你会听到各种有趣的东西开始发生。现在我会在中途关掉白噪声，你就能听到失真单独对低频做了什么，而且你会注意到白噪声其实起了很大作用。

cues.en: Alright. So there's where we go. So I was like, oh man, this is brilliant. Right? Here we go. This is gonna be the doom sound. We're gonna take sine waves. I'm gonna take noise. I'm gonna run them through some distortion. I'm an absolute genius. This is brilliant. So I sent this off to Chris. Right? And I tapped out a really big email justifying the whole thing and I said, this is gonna be awesome. Let this thing blow your mind. And then I sent it off. I sent... Hit send on the email and I waited Chris's reply.
cues.zh: 好。那就往这个方向做。我当时想，天哪，这太棒了。对吧？来吧。这会是 Doom 的声音。我们要取正弦波。我要取噪声。我要把它们过失真。我绝对是个天才。这太棒了。于是我把这个发给 Chris。对吧？我还敲了一封超长的邮件来论证整件事，我说，这会非常棒。让这东西震撼你。然后我发了出去。我发……点了发送邮件，然后等 Chris 回复。

cues.en: He replied with this.
cues.zh: 他回了这个。

cues.en: Now you're only laughing there because you're suffering the same fear of rejection that I am. Right? And there I am. I read that on my screen and I'm like, oh no. I failed again. Right? Time to go turn on the cold water in the shower and have a bit of a cry.
cues.zh: 现在你们笑，只是因为你们和我一样害怕被拒绝。对吧？然后我就在那儿。我在屏幕上读到那个，心想，完了。我又失败了。对吧？该去打开淋浴的冷水，哭一小会儿了。

cues.en: But then underneath that, he had these lines.
cues.zh: 但在那下面，他又写了这几句话。

cues.en: I feel you've taken the first step on a journey toward the perfect destination.
cues.zh: “我觉得你已经迈出了通往完美终点的第一步。

cues.en: Keep going.
cues.zh: 继续加油。

cues.en: You're almost there.
cues.zh: 你就快做到了。”

cues.en: Now instantly,
cues.zh: 就在那一瞬间，

cues.en: I felt comfortable
cues.zh: 我感到能够

cues.en: with failure.
cues.zh: 坦然面对失败了。

cues.en: I wasn't worried about failing with this team.
cues.zh: 我不再担心在这个团队里搞砸。

cues.en: I was encouraged to be able to keep going. Chris understood what I was trying to do here,
cues.zh: 我受到了继续前行的鼓舞。Chris 理解我想做什么，

cues.en: but rather than rejecting it outright and therefore rejecting me and my abilities,
cues.zh: 他没有直接全盘否定，也没有因此否定我和我的能力，

cues.en: he was saying keep going. You're on the right path.
cues.zh: 而是对我说：继续做，你的方向是对的。

cues.en: He was an encouraging... He was encouraging an environment where I felt comfortable in failure.
cues.zh: 他在营造……他在营造一种让我能坦然面对失败的环境。

cues.en: Now it was clear after this that I really wasn't doing the right thing. Right? I knew in myself it wasn't correct. All I'd done is taken some sounds and ran them through distortion. I mean, that's not really amazing. I'm a guitar player and made a living out of doing that exact thing for about ten years.
cues.zh: 事情过后我很清楚自己做得其实并不对。对吧？我自知做得不够好。我只是抓了些声音，加了点失真效果而已。这其实没什么了不起的。我本身就是个吉他手，靠干这行混饭吃了大概十年。

cues.en: But what I needed to do was change the process. Right?
cues.zh: 但我真正需要做的，是改变流程，对吧？

cues.en: Change the process.
cues.zh: 改变流程，

cues.en: Change the outcome.
cues.zh: 就能改变结果。

cues.en: I'm a big fan of Doom three.
cues.zh: 我是 Doom 3 的铁杆粉丝。

cues.en: I really, really quite enjoyed doing Doom three. I really love the darkness that they were able to get into it. I really love storytelling.
cues.zh: 我真的非常享受玩 Doom 3。我很喜欢他们营造出的那种黑暗氛围，也很喜欢那种叙事。

cues.en: I thought it was such an amazing technical achievement that they were able to pull off back in the in 2004.
cues.zh: 我觉得在 2004 年他们能实现这样的效果，真是一项惊人的技术成就。

cues.en: I found it really really quite inspiring. It was an interesting project.
cues.zh: 它真的给了我很多启发。那是个很有意思的项目。

cues.en: Now, of course, the music that you're hearing there,
cues.zh: 当然，你们刚才听到的音乐，

cues.en: Chris Renner
cues.zh: 是 Chris Renner

cues.en: had produced this track for Doom three. Now, Chris is an incredible person. I've only spoken to Chris a couple of times but his high level of music ability is only matched by his personality. He's a really really wonderful person.
cues.zh: 为 Doom 3 制作的。Chris 是个了不起的人。我只和他聊过几次，但他卓越的音乐才华与他的人品一样出众。他真的是个非常好的人。

cues.en: Chris of course played drums among Nine Inch Nails for many years and went on to play with Marilyn Manson and all that sort of stuff. Really, really great guy.
cues.zh: Chris 曾给 Nine Inch Nails 打过很多年鼓，后来还跟 Marilyn Manson 等人合作过。人真的非常棒。

cues.en: But it was his experience with Nine Inch Nails that remembered something. I remembered that at one point, Nine Inch Nails toured with David Bowie.
cues.zh: 正是他在 Nine Inch Nails 的经历让我想起了一件事。我记起 Nine Inch Nails 曾一度和 David Bowie 一起巡演过。

cues.en: Then David Bowie himself is obviously a really incredible musician and this reminded me of an interesting story.
cues.zh: 而 David Bowie 本人显然是一位极其不可思议的音乐家，这也让我想起了一个有趣的故事。

cues.en: Back in 1977
when Bowie was in Berlin recording Heroes,
cues.zh: 当 Bowie 在柏林录制《Heroes》时，

cues.en: he was working with a fascinating
cues.zh: 他正在与一位非常有才华的

cues.en: engineer named
cues.zh: 录音工程师合作，

cues.en: Tony Visconti.
cues.zh: 名字叫 Tony Visconti。

cues.en: Now, to the technical limitations that these guys were working with, they'd only run out... They'd pretty much run out with tracks on this tape machine that they were using. They had one track left for vocals,
cues.zh: 当时由于技术限制，他们用的磁带录音机音轨快……音轨几乎快用完了。只剩下一轨用来录人声，

cues.en: but to get the full emotional impact of this song across, they needed to have reverb that was scalable.
cues.zh: 但为了传达出这首歌全部的情感冲击力，他们需要具备动态缩放能力的混响效果。

cues.en: So Tony, the engineer came up with this really incredible technique.
cues.zh: 于是工程师 Tony 想出了一个非常惊艳的技巧。

cues.en: He set up David Bowie in the middle of the studio here, right at the frontier.
cues.zh: 他把 David Bowie 安排在录音室正中央，就在最前沿。

cues.en: So David would be singing into that microphone.
cues.zh: David 就对着那个麦克风唱。

cues.en: About 20 feet away from that would be a second microphone.
cues.zh: 大概 20 英尺外放了第二个麦克风。

cues.en: Then at the end of the hall was a third microphone.
cues.zh: 然后在大厅尽头放了第三个麦克风。

cues.en: Now microphones two and three at the back there were behind a gate. Alright. Everybody understands what a gate is. Right? Open closed gate, audio gate. Right?
cues.zh: 后方的二号和三号麦克风都加了门限（Gate）。大家都懂门限吧？开、关，音频门限，对吧？

cues.en: Now when David was singing at the start of the song and it was kinda low tones, there wasn't much volume to his voice. So this first microphone was all that was picking up.
cues.zh: 歌曲开头 David 唱得比较低沉时，音量不大，所以只有这第一个麦克风在拾音。

cues.en: Then when he'd open up a little bit, the second microphone, the gate would open and allow some of his voice through. That would create a bit of a natural ambience.
cues.zh: 当他稍微放开一点唱时，第二个麦克风的门限就会打开，收入一部分声音，营造出一点自然的空间氛围感。

cues.en: Then when Bowie would really rip into it, the gate on the third microphone at the back would open up.
cues.zh: 等 Bowie 真正完全爆发开嗓时，最后面第三个麦克风的门限就会彻底打开。

cues.en: And what I thought was really fascinating about this is that they designed a system
cues.zh: 我觉得最绝的是，他们设计了这样一个系统：

cues.en: that dynamically
cues.zh: 它能够

cues.en: added reverb
cues.zh: 动态叠加混响，

cues.en: based on the input.
cues.zh: 完全取决于输入信号。

cues.en: So I thought, well, what if I designed a system
cues.zh: 于是我想，要是我也设计一个系统，

cues.en: that dynamically produced interesting and appropriate musical bits
cues.zh: 能根据输入信号

cues.en: based on the input?
cues.zh: 动态生成有趣且贴切的音乐片段呢？

cues.en: To be inspired by this, I started getting this awesome concept art through for the project.
cues.zh: 为了寻找灵感，我开始接触这个项目超赞的概念原画。

cues.en: I was really fascinated by these concepts of where they had these giant rock structures that were being held together with this evil force of energy, this hell energy.
cues.zh: 我彻底被这些设定迷住了：巨大的岩石结构，被一股邪恶的地狱能量死死维系在一起。

cues.en: And the story in the game is that this evil corporation
cues.zh: 游戏的故事是说，有一家邪恶的大公司，

cues.en: has found a way to mine this energy as a source of renewable energy. Right? Sustainable energy source.
cues.zh: 找到了一种开采这种能量的方法，把它当作可再生能源。对吧？可持续能源。

cues.en: But I kinda love this idea that everything from your mobile phone to the TV you watch to the pacemaker that's keeping you alive to the plane that you're flying is all being powered by energy mind from hell.
cues.zh: 但我很喜欢这个脑洞：从你的手机、看的电视，到维持生命的起搏器，再到你乘坐的飞机，全都是由从地狱开采的能量驱动的。

cues.en: This kind of evil energy. Right?
cues.zh: 就是这种邪恶能量，对吧？

cues.en: I had this idea about this this sort of force that was traveling through things and getting corrupted,
cues.zh: 我当时就想到了这样一种力量，它流经万物，并不断被腐化，

cues.en: this evil energy.
cues.zh: 就是这种邪恶能量。

cues.en: So with that in mind, I set out to design the following system.
cues.zh: 带着这个想法，我开始着手设计下面这套系统。

cues.en: Now for the sake of this next bit,
cues.zh: 接下来为了便于理解，

cues.en: I want you to think of audio
cues.zh: 我希望大家把音频

cues.en: like water.
cues.zh: 想象成水流。

cues.en: It flows downhill.
cues.zh: 水往低处流。

cues.en: We start with the computer at the top.
cues.zh: 我们从最顶端的电脑开始。

cues.en: The computer is what generates the sound. In this case, it was a simple sine wave. We'll go into more of that in a little bit.
cues.zh: 电脑负责发声。在这个案例中，它发出的只是简单的正弦波，我们稍后再详聊。

cues.en: That computer split that signal out into four different paths.
cues.zh: 电脑把这个信号分流成四条不同的路径。

cues.en: These paths went into a chain.
cues.zh: 这些路径进入了一条效果链。

cues.en: The first chain
cues.zh: 第一条链路

cues.en: consisted of a whole bunch of petals. Four pedals as a result. Now for this first test, I actually wrote these down for the real geeks in the audience if you're curious.
cues.zh: 串联了一大堆单块效果器，一共有四个。针对第一次测试，要是现场有极客好奇，我还真把它们记录下来了。

cues.en: So the first pedal there was a Retro Mechanical Labs four three two k distortion box, really really great distortion box.
cues.zh: 第一个单块是 Retro Mechanical Labs 432k 失真效果器，非常非常棒的一款失真单块。

cues.en: The second pedal was a Metasonics k v 100, really interesting tube distortion.
cues.zh: 第二个效果器是 Metasonics KV100，一个很有意思的电子管失真。

cues.en: The third pedal was a Geiger counter. It's like a bit crusher that you can kinda do some cool stuff with. The fourth pedal was a dwarf dwarf, fuzz from the dwarf craft devices guys. They're really, really cool as well.
cues.zh: 第三个效果器是 Geiger Counter。它像个 bit crusher，你可以拿它做一些很酷的东西。第四个效果器是 Dwarf Dwarf，是 Dwarfcraft Devices 那帮人做的法兹。它们也都真的、真的非常酷。

cues.en: That was the first chain. At the bottom of that was a splitter. We'll get back to that one in a second.
cues.zh: 那就是第一条链。它的末端是一个分线器。我们待会儿再回到那个。

cues.en: The second chain went through a very similar setup. We had another four pedals. The first one was another Geiger counter, just for awesomeness.
cues.zh: 第二条链经过了非常相似的设置。我们又有四个效果器。第一个又是一个 Geiger Counter，纯粹为了爽。

cues.en: The second one was a Metasonics t x three. Google it or don't.
cues.zh: 第二个是 Metasonics TX3。去谷歌一下，或者别搜。

cues.en: The third was a Mutron BiPhase, an old phaser from like the late sixties, early seventies, really really old phaser pedal.
cues.zh: 第三个是 Mutron BiPhase，一个六十年代末、七十年代初的老式相位效果器，真的、真的非常老的相位效果器。

cues.en: Because I really liked old phaser pedals, there was a second one of those. It was a Dodge seventies phaser as well. So really, really cool stuff.
cues.zh: 因为我真的很喜欢老式相位效果器，所以又放了一个。它也是 Dodge seventies phaser。所以真是、真是很酷的东西。

cues.en: At the end of that was a compressor. We'll come back to that one in a second.
cues.zh: 它的末端是一个压缩器。我们待会儿再回到那个。

cues.en: The third chain consisted of a tape echo. I had this Watkins copycat
cues.zh: 第三条链包含一个磁带回声。我有一台 Watkins Copycat

cues.en: old tape echo. They would actually record to a tape and then the record head is back with the play head. So whatever you record plays up behind and that says, it's like proper echo, actual natural echo on a on a tape machine. Right? Real stuff.
cues.zh: 老式磁带回声。它会真的录到磁带上，然后录音磁头后面就是放音磁头。所以你录下的东西会在后面播放出来，这就像真正的回声，磁带机上的自然回声。对吧？真家伙。

cues.en: The second distortion
cues.zh: 第二个失真

cues.en: box that was under that, the pedal one that you see listed there on the third chain, that was just another distortion box. It was a Trogatronic
cues.zh: 盒，就在那下面，也就是你在第三条链上看到的那个效果器，那只是另一个失真盒。它是 Trogatronic

cues.en: valve distortion thing. It wasn't really there for the distortion aspect. It was there more for the compression aspect.
cues.zh: 电子管失真的东西。它放在那里其实不是为了失真，更多是为了压缩。

cues.en: After that, I had this old Akai reel to reel machine from the seventies.
cues.zh: 之后，我有一台七十年代的老 Akai 开盘录音机。

cues.en: It's like a tiny little quarter inch thing. Great sound. Really, really grimy.
cues.zh: 它就像个小小的四分之一英寸的东西。声音很棒。真的、真的非常粗粝。

cues.en: What I was doing here was feeding it with about 40 decibels more than it could handle which is really, really cool and then recording back off it at the same time.
cues.zh: 我在这里做的是给它喂比它能承受的高出约 40 分贝的信号，这真的、真的非常酷，然后同时从它那里录回来。

cues.en: Following on to that, that went into a spring reverb tank with a wet and dry control so I could kind of play around with that. That went into a compressor which I'll talk about in a second.
cues.zh: 接着，它进入一个带干湿控制的弹簧混响箱，这样我就能稍微玩一玩。然后它进入一个压缩器，我待会儿会讲到。

cues.en: The final one, we did a couple of different interesting things with. The signal was sent out to a little mini amp. You know those little crappy like Fender mini amp things that got like a tiny little speaker in them?
cues.zh: 最后一个，我们做了几件不同的有趣的事。信号被送到一个小迷你音箱。你知道那种很破的 Fender 迷你小音箱，里面有个很小的喇叭吗？

cues.en: Again, it was being fed with about 40 decibels too much of what it can handle.
cues.zh: 同样，给它喂的信号比它能承受的高了约 40 分贝。

cues.en: This... That was being mic'd with a little, like like a microphone with... So the the speaker,
cues.zh: 这个……它被一个小……就像一个小麦克风……拾音，所以那个喇叭，

cues.en: had a microphone in front of it and a little bit of that signal was being sent through a splitter back into the amp itself. So we're creating a feedback loop there.
cues.zh: 前面放了一个麦克风，然后一点信号通过分线器送回音箱本身。所以我们在那里制造了一个反馈回路。

cues.en: But the feedback loop was only very very small. It was so small that if a sound was actually coming through the amp, it would choke out the feedback. And when that sound started to disappear, the feedback would come back up in the mix. I have a little example of that running here.
cues.zh: 但反馈回路非常非常小。小到如果有声音真的从功放出来，就会把反馈压掉。而当那个声音开始消失时，反馈又会在混音里冒回来。我这里有个小例子正在播放。

cues.en: So when you hear whenever that distortion sort of stuff starts to die out, the feedback comes in. Right?
cues.zh: 所以当你听到那种失真之类的声音开始消失时，反馈就进来了。对吧？

cues.en: So the next thing is that every single one of those ran into a mixer so I could start summing things back down.
cues.zh: 接下来，这些东西每一路都进了一个混音器，这样我就可以开始把声音重新汇总混合下来。

cues.en: That ran into an e q and a compressor. The e q wasn't really doing much. It was adding about four or five decibels down really low, about 30 to 60 hertz. And Then we were adding about the same up about sort of eight to 10, basically creating a nice sort of smiley face e q. Nothing really amazing there.
cues.zh: 那路信号进入了一个 EQ 和一个压缩器。EQ 其实没做太多。它在很低的地方，大概 30 到 60 赫兹，加了四五分贝。然后我们又在高频大概 8 到 10 千赫的位置加了差不多的量，基本上做出一个好看的微笑曲线 EQ。没什么特别惊艳的。

cues.en: That was running into a compressor. This compressor was absolutely freaking pinned. I'm kidding. It was knocking off about 20 decibels. Right? The reason I was hitting it that hard was so when the loud noises would start to go away,
cues.zh: 那信号进入了一个压缩器。这个压缩器简直被压得死死的。开玩笑的。它大概削掉了 20 分贝。对吧？我之所以压得这么狠，是为了当大音量开始消失时，

cues.en: the compressor would begin to open up and bring up all the interesting noise
cues.zh: 压缩器就会开始打开，把那些有趣的噪声都提上来，

cues.en: that every single one of these pedals and bits of equipment was creating. I'll show you more of that in a second. That's very important. The compressor itself was set at about a thirty millisecond attack, so we got some really cool punchy stuff. And then I'd adjust the release based on the tempo of whatever I was sending through it. Again, I'll show you that in more in a second. The ratio was about 12 or 20 to one. Pretty pretty pretty drastic. Pretty crazy.
cues.zh: 这些踏板和设备产生的。我一会儿会多展示一些。这点很重要。压缩器本身起音设在大约 30 毫秒，所以能得到一些很酷、很有冲击力的东西。然后我会根据送进去的内容的节奏来调整释放。这个我一会儿也会再详细展示。压缩比大概是 12 比 1 或 20 比 1。相当相当相当激进。相当疯狂。

cues.en: And that was running straight into the, to the digital audio workstation there and recording stuff.
cues.zh: 然后它直接进入那边的数字音频工作站，开始录音。

cues.en: So what I'm gonna do next is attempt to, if we can get some volume on the, the computer here,
cues.zh: 所以我接下来要做的是，尝试一下——如果我们能让这边电脑发出点声音，

cues.en: I'm gonna show you my first experiment
cues.zh: 我要给你们看我的第一个实验

cues.en: running through this array.
cues.zh: 让它通过这个阵列跑一遍。

cues.en: I'm gonna show you a series of sub sine wave tones.
cues.zh: 我要给你们听一系列低频正弦波音调。

cues.en: They're four f notes followed by a little bit of a gap.
cues.zh: 它们是四个 F 音，后面跟着一小段间隔。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: 它

cues.en: not meant to be buzzing. That's that buzzing over there.
cues.zh: 本不该发出嗡鸣。那是那边那个东西在嗡嗡响。

cues.en: The gap.
cues.zh: 间隔。

cues.en: Okay. So that's it. Now I know what you're thinking. It's really not amazing. Right? I know music of the year right here. Woo.
cues.zh: 好。就是这样。现在我知道你们在想什么。这真的不惊艳。对吧？我知道，年度最佳音乐就在这儿。哇。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: when you run that through this array,
cues.zh: 当你把那段声音通过这个阵列跑一遍，

cues.en: all sorts of interesting stuff starts to happen.
cues.zh: 各种有趣的事情就开始发生。

cues.en: What I want you to listen out for is a couple of things.
cues.zh: 我想让你们注意听的是几件事。

cues.en: At at the end of those four f notes, you'll hear another note creeping underneath.
cues.zh: 在那四个 F 音结束时，你会听到另一个音在底下悄悄冒出来。

cues.en: It's like an e. It's like just below the f.
cues.zh: 它像是一个 E。像是刚好在 F 下面。

cues.en: That's not being generated from me. That's not being generated from the computer. That's coming from some ground within the array.
cues.zh: 那不是由我产生的。也不是由电脑产生的。它来自阵列内部的某个接地处。

cues.en: Additional to that, there's all sorts of interesting distortion layers that are coming in and out based on that splitter on the left hand side there that was sending a signal to those compressors along the bottom.
cues.zh: 除此之外，基于左边那个分流器把信号发送给底部的压缩器，会有各种有趣的失真层若隐若现。

cues.en: Sometimes if I wanted to, that was essentially side chaining the signal from those other chains.
cues.zh: 有时只要我想，这实质上就是对来自其他链路的信号做侧链处理。

cues.en: So based on whatever the input what it was... Sorry. Based on whatever the input was doing, it could dynamically change the mix of which... Whatever each chain I had.
cues.zh: 所以根据输入的……抱歉，根据输入信号的不同表现，它可以动态改变每个……各个链路的混音比例。

cues.en: The last thing I want you to hear out for is all sorts of interesting stuff that's going on with the sonics and things. You'll hear all sorts of harmonics.
cues.zh: 最后我还希望大家留意听一下声音细节上的各种奇妙变化，你能听到各种泛音。

cues.en: Anyway, here again is that same subwoofer tone run through this array several times.
cues.zh: 总之，这里还是那个超低音音色，只是多次经过了这个效果器阵列。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: we're getting somewhere interesting.
cues.zh: 事情变得有趣起来了。

cues.en: So the way I started thinking about this was that this was my instrument.

cues.en: So what did we learn on to? Well,
cues.zh: 那我们学到了什么？嗯，

cues.en: if you want to get a different outcome,
cues.zh: 如果你想得到不同的结果，

cues.en: you must change the process.
cues.zh: 你就必须改变过程。

cues.en: Change the process.
cues.zh: 改变过程。

cues.en: Change the outcome.
cues.zh: 改变结果。

cues.en: If you're struggling to come up with something new,
cues.zh: 如果你很难想出新的东西，

cues.en: if you find yourself stuck in a rut, if you're suffering from creative blocks,
cues.zh: 如果你发现自己陷入一成不变，如果你遭遇创意瓶颈，

cues.en: change the process.
cues.zh: 改变过程。

cues.en: Change the way you're doing things and you'll end up with a different result.
cues.zh: 改变你做事情的方式，你最终就会得到不同的结果。

cues.zh: 不仅如此，还要有勇气

cues.en: to do so.
cues.zh: 去这么做。

cues.zh: 我说的是勇气，

cues.en: not confidence.
cues.zh: 不是自信。

cues.zh: 自信来自一遍又一遍又一遍又一遍地做同样的事。

cues.en: It takes courage to change that.
cues.zh: 要改变这一点，需要勇气。

cues.zh: 我们学到的第二件事：如果能让项目更好，就改项目简报。

cues.zh: 尽管简报说不要用吉他，而我们一开始也走了那条路，

cues.en: we felt comfortable changing that later on to satisfy a more important element of that brief.
cues.zh: 后来我们觉得可以放心地改掉这一点，以满足简报中更重要的部分。

cues.en: Sometimes you cannot do everything.
cues.zh: 有时候你不可能面面俱到。

cues.en: That being said though, I feel we reached a more interesting place
cues.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得我们到达了一个更有趣的境地

cues.en: by ignoring the guitar element that was so synonymous with the doom the doom universe to begin with.
cues.zh: 通过忽略吉他元素——它原本与 DOOM 宇宙如此密不可分。

cues.en: I feel if we started with guitars in mind,
cues.zh: 我觉得如果我们一开始就想着吉他，

cues.zh: 我们最终做出来的东西就会像我之前播放的那些梗一样。

cues.zh: 最后，也是最重要的一点，

cues.en: a team that encourages an environment
cues.zh: 一个鼓励营造这样一种环境的团队

cues.zh: 让你在失败中也感到自在

cues.en: will enable you to thrive.
cues.zh: 才能让你茁壮成长。

cues.zh: 去再多推一点边界。

cues.zh: 我们常说，做项目时，你一方面要提供音乐

cues.zh: 一方面也要做音乐的教育者。

cues.zh: 试着去教育你的上级、下属和同级团队成员，然后，一个鼓励你失败、也让你觉得失败没关系的环境

cues.en: Hey, man. This is brilliant by the way. Thank you.
cues.zh: 嘿，哥们。顺便说一句，这太棒了。谢谢。

cues.en: One of my favorite things about your music both in Doom and in Killer Instinct is how it's integrated to kind of respond to player actions and player input.
cues.zh: 你的音乐在 Doom 和 Killer Instinct 里，我最喜欢的一点是它如何被整合起来，对玩家的动作和输入做出响应。

cues.en: Like in Doom, the the glory kills cause some of your music to muffle and distort And then in Killer Instinct, you've got those ultra combos that
cues.zh: 比如在 Doom 里，荣耀击杀会让你的部分音乐变得沉闷、失真；而在 Killer Instinct 里，那些 Ultra Combo 会

cues.en: completely
cues.zh: 完全

cues.en: changes the music, in real time. And I'm curious, do you have a hand in some of that integration?
cues.zh: 实时改变音乐。我很好奇，你有参与其中一些整合吗？

cues.en: And can you talk a little bit about the differences between
cues.zh: 能不能稍微谈谈……之间的区别

cues.en: this project and Killer Instinct? Yeah. Sure. Absolutely. Really, really good question.
cues.zh: 这个项目和 Killer Instinct？是。当然。完全可以。非常好的问题。

cues.en: The reason I chose not to kinda go too much into the implementation side of things on Doom is that there's a lot of questions and things here that usually happens at GDC about this which allows me to answer those sort of things. But not only that, there's a lot of talks that kinda go into the implementation side of it as well. And I found that there were some really important lessons that I learned on the doom score such as the team that really encourages an environment where you feel comfortable in failing that were kinda really important that you don't really see discussed
cues.zh: 我选择不在 Doom 的实现细节上讲太多，是因为通常 GDC 上有很多关于这方面的问题和内容，让我可以回答这类问题。不仅如此，很多演讲也会深入讲它的实现侧。而且我发现，我在 Doom 配乐中学到了一些非常重要的经验，比如团队真正鼓励一种让你不怕失败的环境，这些其实很重要，却很少看到被讨论

cues.en: in GDC.
cues.zh: 在 GDC 上。

cues.en: So thanks so much for answering this question.
cues.zh: 非常感谢你回答这个问题。

cues.en: Essentially, the biggest difference between Killer Instinct and Doom is obviously the style of the game. Killer Instinct has a very predictable structure where you're going to have a first round, a second round. You know, there's a kills at the end. There's combos that can happen. This is kind of framework that you're working within.
cues.zh: 本质上，Killer Instinct 和 Doom 最大的区别显然是游戏风格。Killer Instinct 的结构非常可预测，你会有一回合、第二回合。你知道，最后会有击杀，会有连招发生。这就是你所处的一种框架。

cues.en: Doom essentially pretty much every battle in Doom is is a linear path. Right? You enter the arena, the demons come out.
cues.zh: Doom 本质上……在 Doom 里几乎每场战斗都是一条线性路径。对吧？你进入竞技场，恶魔出来。

cues.en: Your role is to kill all the demons and then you kind of move forward. It's this very kind of linear progression.
cues.zh: 你的任务就是干掉所有恶魔，然后继续前进，这是一种非常线性的推进流程。

cues.en: Now, we chose not to do too much crazy dynamic music stuff within that structure because it just seemed to get into the way of the groove.
cues.zh: 在这种结构下，我们选择不做太多花哨的动态音乐，因为那似乎会打乱整体的律动感。

cues.en: Basically, when that player started and those demons came in, we just wanted it to be on. Just on just going just bang bang bang bang bang. Just like you've jumped in the car and you hit play on that that album. Right? You're just going. You're off off.
cues.zh: 简单来说，只要玩家一进场、恶魔一刷新，我们就要音乐立刻炸裂，直接燥起来，砰砰砰一路狂飙；就像你跳上车猛按播放键放那张专辑一样，对吧？整个人直接嗨起来、冲出去。

cues.en: So that was the biggest thing. There was a couple of little things that we did. Obviously, when you do the glory kills, the music drops out and there's a little riser
cues.zh: 所以那是核心思路。不过我们也做了一些细节调整。显然，当你进行壮烈击杀时，音乐会骤降，紧接着会有一个小小的升音

cues.en: that happens.
cues.zh: 出现。

cues.en: We didn't really know how long each glory kill was going to take, so I made a series of what I call endless rises.
cues.zh: 因为我们没法确切知道每次壮烈击杀会持续多久，所以我做了一系列被我称为“无尽升音”的效果。

cues.en: These are essentially looping rises. Now, I know that's a break in terminology but let me explain it. Basically, we're taking a shepherd's tone. You ever know what a shepherd tone is? Yeah.
cues.zh: 它们本质上是循环升音。我知道这在术语上不太严谨，但容我解释一下。基本上，我们借用了谢泼德音（Shepard Tone）的原理。大家知道什么是谢泼德音吗？是的。

cues.en: Okay. Basically, it's just taking a series of notes that go from low to high. Right? When those notes are coming in high,
cues.zh: 好的。基本上，它就是让一组音符由低向高走，对吧？当这些音符升到高音区时，

cues.en: you're kind of fading in the the lower notes again. It's a little bit more complicated than that. I really encourage you to jump on Google and check it out. It's a really interesting thing. But if you use this philosophy, can create these looping rises. It just feels constantly like there's this tension rising. It's really really handy in game environments when you're stuck in a situation where you don't know how long something is going to go for. So we did that.
cues.zh: 你又会把低音部分悄悄淡入。实际原理要复杂一些，强烈建议大家去 Google 搜一下看看，真的非常有趣。但只要运用这种思路，就能做出这种循环升音。它会让人感觉紧张感在不断攀升。在游戏开发中，如果你遇到无法预知持续时长的场景，这种做法超级实用。所以我们就这么干了。

cues.en: And then other times, we started to experiment with this idea of like the music had started and like there was the high hat and the basic riff kicking along and then bam, when everything kicked in, that's when the music would start and that's when it really kick in. cues.zh: 还有些时候，我们尝试了另一种思路：音乐先响起来，踩镲和基础 riff 跟着走，然后“砰”的一声，当所有元素一齐爆发时，音乐才真正火力全开。坦白讲，这就是 Doom 里的动态音乐系统全部的复杂度了。至于交付给团队的方式，我通常把曲子分轨拆解开，导入到 Wwise 里，然后把 Wwise 工程文件发给团队。我拆分出来的部分主要就是

cues.en: So first of all, the setup that you made Yes. You use sine waves. Right? Yes. Didn't you... Did you experiment with saw waves, square waves just to get more harmonics? Yeah. Interesting. So the first thing there basically everything started as a sine wave.
cues.zh: 首先，你搭建的那套设备——对。——你用的是正弦波，对吧？——对。——你有没有……试过锯齿波、方波来获得更多谐波吗？——嗯，很有意思。首先，基本上所有声音最开始都是正弦波。

cues.en: What I wanted to do as I said as I said before is to kind of capture whatever the pedal was going to add to it. Mhmm.
